## Paramedic Salary Adelaide: From Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you are looking at a paramedic salary Adelaide, the first step is to understand how your hourly rate translates into annual earnings. Whether you are a full-time, part-time, or casual paramedic, the calculation is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you your gross annual salary before tax and super.

### The Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For example, if your base hourly rate is $35 and you work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. This formula works for any hourly rate. If you are a casual paramedic, you add a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate before doing the multiplication. Remember, the loading is extra – you never type a rate that already includes casual loading into our [timesheet](/). Instead, check the box to add 25% on top.

### Award Rates for Paramedics in Adelaide

Paramedics in Adelaide are covered by the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that list the minimum rates for each classification. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, but award rates are typically higher. For example, a qualified paramedic may have a base rate above $30 per hour. Casual paramedics receive a 25% loading, making their casual rate $33.05 per hour or more, depending on the classification. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database also contains detailed rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Use these official sources to confirm your correct rate.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

Many employers pay fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. For a full-time paramedic on $35 per hour, weekly pay is $1,330, so fortnightly is $2,660. If you are casual, add the 25% loading first. This helps you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly amounts.

## Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Two important concepts affect your total compensation: casual loading and superannuation.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees do not receive paid sick leave or annual leave. To compensate, the award requires a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This loading is paid on top of the ordinary rate. For example, if the base rate is $30, the casual rate becomes $37.50. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it correctly. Always start with the base award rate, then add the loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading into the timesheet.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top, Not Deducted

Superannuation is an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer into a super fund. It is not taken out of your pay. For the 2026-27 year, the super guarantee rate is 12%, and it applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a paramedic earning $69,160 gross, the employer contributes an extra $8,299.20 per year. This is separate from your take-home pay. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your gross annual salary, you can estimate your tax. The 2026-27 resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Most people also pay a 2% Medicare levy. For a paramedic earning $69,160, the tax would be approximately $11,067 plus Medicare of $1,383, leaving a take-home pay of about $56,710. This is an estimate – your actual tax depends on your circumstances. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised calculation.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It is important to know the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading. The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor: $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher and specific to each industry. For paramedics, the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award sets the minimum. Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the award rate. Super is paid on top of all these. Never confuse the base rate with the casual rate. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page explains the current rates.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Paramedic Salary Adelaide

Our [timesheet](/) is designed to help you convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Start with your base hourly rate from the award. If you are casual, tick the casual loading checkbox – the tool adds 25% automatically. Then enter your hours per week (38 for full-time). The tool calculates gross annual pay, fortnightly pay, and an estimate of tax and super. Remember, the results are estimates. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. For a precise paramedic salary Adelaide, always refer to your employment contract and the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog).

## Final Thoughts

Understanding your paramedic salary Adelaide starts with knowing your hourly rate, applying the correct loading, and adding super. Use the official award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. The Australian Taxation Office also provides guidance on deductions for paramedics, such as uniforms and travel. With the right tools, you can confidently estimate your annual pay and plan your finances.
